# Pinned Nostr dependency

This directory contains the production package closure used by Holoboard from
`fiatjaf.com/nostr v0.0.0-20261005012418-685c38fc6629`
(commit `685c38fc6629d20a838aaf1b114919cfed1dc866`), including Khatru.
The upstream Unlicense, go.mod and go.sum are retained. Unused subpackages,
examples and public-network tests are omitted. Deterministic event, envelope,
filter, tag, encoding, NIP-04 and NIP-44 tests are included with their fixtures.

The [source manifest](SOURCE.json) hashes every retained upstream file.
The [local patch](../../patches/nostr-holoboard.patch) contains all source
differences and local regression tests. Follow the
[verification procedure](../../patches/README.md) when refreshing this snapshot.

## Required differences

The successor does not replace Holoboard's transport and admission policies.
The local patch retains joined connection shutdown, bounded subscription
admission, synchronous event delivery with backpressure, a 1 MiB decompressed
message limit, shared receive admission and partial results with query errors.
EOSE is received from the relay, never generated by a local timer. A query
retains at most 512 events or 4 MiB. Subscriptions support up to eight filters
on one NIP-01 request. Cancellation serializes cleanup after an in-flight REQ.
Publish acknowledgements are bounded and removed on every exit path.

Khatru processes each socket's frames in order, limits clients, filters,
listeners, stored-query workers and received traffic, and cancels stored
queries on CLOSE. Listener snapshots and changes share one lock. Broadcasts
apply the full filter, including IDs. Standard HTTP startup/shutdown helpers,
payment-compatible timeouts, NIP-11 Accept negotiation and service URL
initialization preserve the application's existing server behavior.

Event validation binds the supplied ID and signature to the body, including
NIP-42 authentication. Canonical serialization and streaming hashes escape
backspace and form feed as required by NIP-01. Input decoding validates hex
with Go's standard decoder, rejects overflowing kinds and checks lengths
before unsafe conversions. Outbound envelope IDs are JSON-escaped.

The application's own connection manager injects a DNS-pinned HTTP transport
and disables WebSocket redirects. Existing API fields, tags and ledger keys
use explicit hexadecimal strings. Unknown event fields are retained across
ledger saves, while canonical hashes include only the NIP-01 signed fields. Signing, encryption and key derivation use
upstream cryptographic implementations. The old NIP-44 nonce workaround is
unnecessary with this revision. The old gobwas PMCE Flush patch is retired
because this client uses coder/websocket; compression interoperability remains
covered against fasthttp/websocket.

The application does not use the upstream pool, automatic auth callback,
negentropy, or additional event stores. Retaining source dependencies is not
a claim that unused features passed Holoboard's acceptance checks. Prefer the
shared application transport when adding reads.

## Regression checks

From `relay/`, include the nested module explicitly:

```sh
GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -race -p 1 -count=1 -timeout=8m ./... fiatjaf.com/nostr/...
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /tmp/holoboard-relay .
```

These checks use local relays and generated test keys. No live wallet payment
or public publication is needed. See [the Nostr reference](../../../docs/nostr.md)
for limits, application contracts and remaining delivery stages.
